terms.gloss: a member of a club or society; a mate
terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
evidence: Dig. 47.22.4: sodālēs sunt, quī ejusdem collēgiī sunt (Lewis & Short, as Dig. 47.12.4)
Cic. Cael. 26: sodālēs in Lupercīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A member of a sodālitās or collēgium; also simply a friend, a mate (see friend).

terms.gloss: to be one of, to be a member of (+ genitive)
evidence: Caes. BG 7.75.4: quō sunt in numerō Curiosolitēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Counting someone a member: in hostium numerō habēre (Caes. BG 1.28, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a partner, a member of a partnership; an ally
a limb; of a person, a member of a body or circle
terms.register: in hōc sēnsū vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.
evidence: Ov. Tr. 4.10.48: dulcia convictūs membra fuēre meī
terms.comment: Of persons first in poetry and in Seneca (membra et partēs, Ep. 21.6, Lewis & Short); in Christian Latin the members of Christ’s body, the Church.

phrases.english: (they) were dear members of my circle

sources: Lewis & Short: sodalis · Lewis & Short: numerus · Lewis & Short: socius · Lewis & Short: membrum
